subject: Sentinel: expedited ask — tenant residency + graceful fallback commitment
messages:
From: Diego Fernandez <diego_fernandez@redwood.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>, Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.com>
Cc: 
Date: Tue, 02 Mar 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Sentinel deal — request to prioritize tenant residency + graceful fallback (time sensitive)

Team,

Quick ask — Sentinel Health (Eva Jenkins) is on a term sheet for ~ $1.1M ARR. They have a hard requirement in procurement: per-tenant model residency (US-only) plus an automated graceful fallback to a compatible quantized variant when capacity or latency SLOs are at risk. Procurement wants this callout in the contract and the customer expects a pilot before they sign (they're slated to legal next Tuesday).

Why this matters: Without a clear residency+fallback commitment we lose the deal. They also require traceability for requests routed outside the tenant pool (audit log entry).

Can Eng/Product evaluate whether we can:
- commit to a pilot that pins model residency to a US tenant pool and exposes a policy-driven fallback to a quantized model variant if capacity thresholds hit, by ~ 2027-04-18, OR
- provide a short-term workaround: dedicated reserved pool for Sentinel (higher cost) that we can stand up faster (~2 weeks) while we build the policy automation.

Attachments: Sentinel_MutualActionPlan.xlsx (MAP), Sentinel_SOC2_scope.pdf (SOC2 excerpt from the customer).

Please reply with feasibility, rough ETA, and any gating risks. This is deal-breaker; happy to set up a 30-min sync.

Thanks,
Diego
Account Executive, Redwood Inference

From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
To: Diego Fernandez <diego_fernandez@redwood.com>, Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 03 Mar 2027 10:08:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Sentinel deal — request to prioritize tenant residency + graceful fallback (time sensitive)

Diego — thanks for flagging. A few clarifying Qs before we commit Prod/Eng cycles: 

1) By "model residency" does Sentinel mean a dedicated tenant pool (isolated infra + data) or just policy-based routing to a region-bound pool?
2) Expected QPS/peak concurrency and token/sec estimates for the pilot (we need to size cache/KV and autoscaling).
3) Does "graceful fallback" require transparent model variant mapping (same API surface + reduced context) or are minor output differences acceptable?
4) Audit logging spec — do they require per-request trace IDs stored for >90 days or just an exportable audit log on demand?

Cc'ing Dev for feasibility. If useful, I can join the customer call.

-Ben
Product Manager, Redwood Inference

From: Diego Fernandez <diego_fernandez@redwood.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>
Cc: Eva Jenkins <eva.jenkins@sentinelhealth.com>, Sentinel Legal <legal@sentinelhealth.com>
Date: Wed, 03 Mar 2027 11:02:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Sentinel deal — request to prioritize tenant residency + graceful fallback (time sensitive)

Ben / Dev — answers from the customer (pulled from today's call with Eva):
- Residency: They need logical isolation and firm statement that model artifacts and runtime for their account will only be in the US region; they will not accept routing to shared international pools. They are okay with a Redwood-managed tenant pool dedicated to their account (not necessarily a single machine).
- Scale: Pilot traffic ~ 40 requests/sec peak, typical prompt lengths 400-600 tokens, 2–3k tokens/day/account estimated. Peak concurrency ~ 12–15 concurrent sessions.
- Fallback expectations: They want the same API surface. Minor output variance is acceptable (they explicitly said quantized/ distilled variant is fine) as long as latency/availability SLOs are preserved and we document the fallback behavior.
- Audit: They require per-request audit metadata (trace id, routed model variant, region, timestamp) and an exportable log covering 30 days.

The customer is willing to accept a pilot (non-production) commitment for the contract if we can show a test harness demonstrating residency + fallback and provide the audit export. They move to legal next Tue (2027-03-09).

Diego

From: Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.com>
To: Diego Fernandez <diego_fernandez@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 04 Mar 2027 09:20:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Sentinel deal — request to prioritize tenant residency + graceful fallback (time sensitive)

Thanks — good summary and helpful constraints. Quick feasibility take (high level):

Approach A (fast, higher cost): provision a Dedicated reserved pool for Sentinel in the US region and route their traffic there. Pros: very little SW change, quicker timeline (~10–14 business days to spin infra + routing + audit hooks). Cons: higher run cost and operational ownership (we need capacity reservation).

Approach B (preferred long-term): implement tenant-label routing + policy-driven fallback to a quantized variant + audit export. Work required:
- Router changes to pin tenancy to US-only pools and emit per-request trace metadata (1 sprint).
- Model variant mapping and runtime fallback (2 sprints, add KV/cache invalidation paths).
- Audit export pipeline (1 sprint, small infra work).

Rough ETA: Pilot-ready for Approach B in ~3 sprints (9 weeks) from start of work — target pilot date ~2027-04-18 is tight but potentially achievable if we scope pilot (limited concurrency and test harness only).

Gating/risk:
- Cache/KV invalidation is the biggest unknown: switching variants mid-session while preserving KV state will need careful gating (may require session-level bucketization).
- Telemetry/exporting 30-day audit is straightforward but we need legal review for retention policies.

Workarounds: we can offer Approach A to buy time; if the customer signs reserved capacity we can meet their legal timeline and then run Approach B in parallel to replace the reserved pool.

I'll draft a short engineering scope (design doc + minimal acceptance tests) today and share a sketch. If Product/Leadership want to accelerate, we need a short-term commitment to allocate 2 backend engineers and 1 infra engineer for the next 6 weeks.

-Dev
Senior Engineer, Serving Runtime

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Diego Fernandez <diego_fernandez@redwood.com>, Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 04 Mar 2027 17:45:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Sentinel deal — request to prioritize tenant residency + graceful fallback (time sensitive)

Team — appreciate the quick analysis. Given deal economics and the strategic nature of a healthcare customer in the US, I authorize the following: 

1) Offer Sentinel a short-term dedicated reserved pool (Approach A) to meet their legal timeline and procurement needs. Diego — include this in the SOW as "pilot reserved capacity."
2) Simultaneously accelerate Approach B as a medium-term product improvement. Dev — please prioritize the design doc and acceptance criteria; Product (Ben) to scope minimal MVP for the pilot that demonstrates residency, fallback, and audit export.
3) Commercial — offer a 20% first-year discount contingent on a 12-month reserved capacity commitment from Sentinel and signed SOW by 2027-03-15. Sales to own negotiation.

Diego: please get a draft SOW to me and legal by EOD tomorrow. Monica: loop in Security/Compliance to validate the SOC2 scope in the attachment.

We should avoid promising GA timelines in the contract; phrase as "pilot demonstration of residency + fallback with audit export."

Marissa Cole
VP, Enterprise Sales
Redwood Inference
